questions.q: What is the problem with the prompt "Summarize this article" on its own?
options: It's an example of ambiguous instructions — length, audience, and format are all left unstated
It will always be rejected by the model as too short
It asks for two incompatible things at once
It contains a factual error about the article
questions.explain: The prompt never specifies length, audience, or format, so the model fills those gaps with its own defaults — an ambiguous-instruction failure.

questions.q: Why does "Be extremely detailed, but keep your answer under 50 words" tend to produce inconsistent results?
options: It's a missing-output-format failure
The two requirements conflict, and the model has to silently pick a winner each time
The word "detailed" is not a word models recognize
50 words is too long for any model to generate
questions.explain: "Extremely detailed" and "under 50 words" can't both be fully satisfied for most topics, so the model resolves the conflict inconsistently run to run.

questions.q: What fix does this lesson give for a prompt whose output format varies from run to run, like "List the three biggest risks"?
options: Add more adjectives to make the request sound more urgent
State the exact structure wanted, e.g. a JSON array of three strings with no other text
Repeat the instruction three times in the same prompt
Remove all punctuation from the prompt
questions.explain: Explicitly naming the exact output shape (such as a JSON array) removes the ambiguity that causes format drift between runs.

questions.q: What happens when a single prompt tries to extract data, summarize, translate, and format all at once?
options: The model automatically splits it into four separate calls on its own
Quality tends to drop across all four tasks as the model's attention divides between them
The model only performs the first task listed and ignores the rest
Nothing changes — a model handles any number of tasks in one prompt equally well
questions.explain: Overloading one prompt with several unrelated jobs tends to reduce quality on each one; splitting into separate prompts (or a chain) usually works better.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what do all four failure modes have in common?
options: They only happen with very old or outdated models
They are caused by using too many words in the prompt
They always require a complete rewrite of the prompt to fix
A decision was left open in the prompt, so the model made it for you — differently than expected
questions.explain: Each failure mode traces back to the same root cause: an unresolved decision in the prompt that the model had to resolve on its own.
